chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from some of our companions from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn Bilal who said:

I wrote to the man asking him about the Fitrah (alms of fasting) and how much should be paid. He wrote back: Six Artals of dates in the Madani measure, and that is nine Artals in the Baghdadi measure.

key_terms.أَرطَال: Artal, a unit of weight measurement used in historical Islamic contexts
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah (alms of fasting), a charitable payment due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.بالبَغْدَادِي: In the Baghdadi measure (referring to the standard weight in Baghdad)
key_terms.بالمَدَنِي: In the Madani measure (referring to the standard weight in Medina)

ai.seo_question: How much Fitrah should be paid in dates according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain establishes the specific weight of dates for Zakat al-Fitr, illustrating the practical application of the Medina Sa' in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the scholarly method of reconciling regional weight discrepancies, noting that six Artals in Medina equates to nine Artals in Baghdad, thereby ensuring the obligation is met according to local standards.
